The section was reopened whole: the sentence's "therefore" refers back to a paragraph that is modern-critical from end to end - "almost a consensus of scientific opinion", "Assyriologists and Egyptologists agree" citing Driver's "Genesis", Ramses II "from 1348-1281 (Sayce)", the concession "we are left with only about 327 years, as against 480 required by 1 Kings 6:1", and "Wellhausen and Stade regard 6:1, as a late insertion" - while of the Catholic reading Howlett says the opposite, "For the Catholic, that passage seems to settle the question." Section 4.3's reporting licence is granted to Ussher BY NAME and to nothing else, which is why claim #2 on this event, Howlett printing Ussher's 1010, stands and this one cannot; `alternate` is a disposition among claims already admitted and opens no admission route. The ruling was NOT confined to #5: the same sentence supplies 1002 and 962, still held on david-accession and solomon-accession, and the immediately following section derives 969, 936 and 937 from it - "the foundation of the Temple may be fixed, according to Sayce, for about the year 969, which would be very near the date given above" - inside a section whose stated project is Mangenot's that the chronology of the kings "must be made to accord with the Assyrian chronology". Withdrawing one figure of that chain while keeping the others would have rebuilt the defect the row condemns, so all six went. Every withdrawn figure is recorded in its subject's note, in the shape israel.exodus.the-exodus's note already uses; the corpus does not lose the fact that Howlett printed them.

column11: The audit's shape is applied, because the ground the earlier ledger gave for withdrawing the finding is false. That ledger says "an event must carry a non-empty dates list, so dropping the claim would mean deleting the event and orphaning its bindings". The loader says otherwise: _claims is called with required=False for events and returns () for a MISSING dates key, and the non-empty raise fires only on a key present and empty. The precedent was live in the same file when the ledger was written - israel.monarchy.saul-accession has stood claimless since ec0020012, which landed BEFORE the commit that created the ledger. The two precedents the ledger cited do not support the stored shape either: ark-comes-to-cariathiarim and division-of-the-land both anchor on an ANTECEDENT event, never on their own container. So the claim is withdrawn, the containment stays where it belongs on `parent`, and the verbatim Ezech. 24:16-18 testimony and the Schets quotation are carried in the event note. Nothing is orphaned: the narrated-event binding survives and already held those words. No gaps.yaml row is authored and none may be - validate refuses an undated-in-tradition row over loci that carry five assertions, and Ezech.24.18 still answers `dated` from the inherited Ezech-scoped claims.

For a more complete list, please see the full index for G [N] or use the search box at the top of this page." The unabridged pages they name were fetched and registered: g-ce.htm, 91589 bytes, 540 article links, no disclaimer, and the Gene- run carries no entry for the book and the string "Genesis" nowhere; n-ce.htm, 42014 bytes, 287 article links, no disclaimer, and "Numbers" occurs once in the whole page, as Thurston's 11151a. Four index-control passage records were added on the corpus's own precedent - each recording the exact inspected run, the page's own disclaimer or its absence, and what the record can and cannot bear. column11: The three keys are deleted, keeping the occurrence the corpus's own key order uses (a census of 464 claims finds 393 in `basis > sources > note > date` order and 158 dates in `precision > from > label`). More importantly the gate exists: the loader now parses every chronology document through a SafeLoader subclass whose construct_mapping records repeated keys at any depth, and refuses the file - naming the path, the line and the key - BEFORE the schema check and before any value is read as a fact. It is installed at _document, the single funnel every one of the five files and every consumer passes through, so no reader can bypass it; it rides the existing parse rather than scanning the bytes twice; and it adds no dependency, PyYAML being the only one the tool has. A wider sweep of all 31 YAML files in the repository and 11 changed TOML files found no other duplicate, and the corpus at 2330d63a5 scans clean, so this is the signature of one edit technique - insert-without-delete by string replacement - and not a systemic corpus problem. That is why the gate, and not the three rows, is the deliverable.
